original_question: If X is a cubic threefold and Ku(X) is the Kuznetsov component appearing in the standard semiorthogonal decomposition of Db(X), is Ku(X) indecomposable?
target_in_paper: Question 3.13 in Section 3.3: the indecomposability of the Kuznetsov component of a cubic threefold.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact problem asked in the paper: it is about a cubic threefold X, its Kuznetsov component Ku(X) inside the standard semiorthogonal decomposition of D^b(X), and whether Ku(X) is indecomposable. This is essentially Question 3.13 verbatim, just with more of the surrounding notation spelled out.
missing_details: X should be specified as a smooth cubic hypersurface in P^4, since that is what the paper means by a cubic threefold in this context.
The ambient field should be stated: throughout the paper varieties are over an algebraically closed field K, and Section 3.3 works in that setting.

The definition of Ku(X) should be made explicit via the canonical semiorthogonal decomposition D^b(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H_X)⟩, where H_X is the primitive ample generator of Pic(X), i.e. the hyperplane class.
The meaning of 'indecomposable' should be unpacked as 'admits no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition,' which the paper explicitly clarifies in footnote 2 near Question 3.9.
To make the question fully stand-alone, the quantifier should be explicit: the question is whether this holds for every such cubic threefold X.
refined_question: For every smooth cubic threefold X ⊂ P^4 over an algebraically closed field K, let Ku(X) be the Kuznetsov component in the canonical semiorthogonal decomposition D^b(X)=⟨Ku(X), O_X, O_X(H_X)⟩, where H_X is the hyperplane class. Is the triangulated category Ku(X) indecomposable, i.e. does it admit no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition?
equivalent_formulation: For a smooth cubic threefold X, does the Kuznetsov component Ku(X) admit any nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition?
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper’s official formulation. The exact target is Question 3.13, asked immediately after Proposition 3.12, which states that for a cubic threefold X the category Ku(X) is fractional Calabi–Yau of fractional dimension 5/3; the indecomposability question is posed as the natural next question. To make the draft fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one should add the global field convention from Section 1.1, the local Section 3.3 setup that cubic threefolds are smooth degree-3 hypersurfaces in P^4, the precise semiorthogonal decomposition defining Ku(X), and the paper’s explicit meaning of 'indecomposable' as 'having no nontrivial semiorthogonal decomposition.' I did not broaden the problem to later stability-condition questions in Section 6, because those are different questions, even though Proposition 3.12 is reused there.
